standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the two ring maps and their uniqueness.

core_obligations: Set up the two pairs produced by the construction from the two ideals (proof lines 3220-3222).
Use the equality of vanishing loci to see that each is henselian with respect to the other's ideal (proof lines 3223-3225).
Apply the universal property to obtain maps in both directions (proof lines 3226-3227).
Conclude by uniqueness that the maps are mutually inverse (proof lines 3228-3229).
proof_roadmap: Universal property gives mutually inverse maps (proof lines 3226-3229).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the henselization constructed from a pair depends only on the radical of the ideal: two ideals with the same vanishing locus give the same ring. The statement carries a slogan recording this dependence. The proof compares the two constructed rings: each is henselian with respect to the other's ideal because the ideals have the same radical, and the universal property of the construction produces ring maps between them in both directions, which are mutually inverse by uniqueness in that universal property.
